skill.name: test-driven-development

security_audit.summary: The static command and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline examples, and ordinary testing language. I found one semantic issue: repeated instructions to delete implementation code and start over can cause destructive edits without explicit confirmation. No evidence of prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before deleting existing implementation code. Reframe non-TDD work as code to review, cover with tests, or rewrite only after approval.
State that test commands are examples and should run only in the user project with normal command-approval safeguards.

content.value_statement: Teams often ship code before tests prove the behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a strict red-green-refactor workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides red-green-refactor work for features, bug fixes, and refactors.
Requires a failing test before production implementation code.
Provides TypeScript examples for clear behavior-focused tests.
Shows local test verification steps using npm test examples.
Includes a completion checklist for test failure, passing tests, and clean output.
References common testing anti-patterns for mocks and test-only methods.
limitations: It does not configure a specific test framework for a project.
It assumes the user wants strict TDD for most coding tasks.
Its deletion guidance needs explicit user approval before removing existing work.
It focuses on test workflow, not full software architecture review.

use_cases.title: Add a New Feature
use_cases.description: Write the expected behavior as a failing test before adding implementation code.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression
use_cases.description: Capture the bug with a failing test, then implement the smallest passing fix.

use_cases.title: Review Testing Discipline
use_cases.description: Check whether a change followed TDD, covered edge cases, and avoided mock-heavy tests.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill. Help me add this small behavior by writing the failing test first, then the minimum implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Reproduce a Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill. Turn this bug report into a failing regression test before proposing the fix.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill. Identify the existing behavior tests first, then guide a refactor that keeps every test green.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill. Review this planned change for missing failing tests, unclear behavior, over-mocking, and unsafe shortcuts.

output_examples.input: Add retry behavior to a failed operation.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the expected retry rule, writes one failing behavior test, confirms the failure reason, then implements only that rule.

output_examples.input: Fix a form that accepts an empty email address.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates a regression test for the empty email case, verifies it fails, adds validation, and confirms the suite passes.

output_examples.input: Review tests that rely heavily on mocks.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies mock assertions, suggests testing real behavior, and recommends lower-level test doubles only where isolation is necessary.

best_practices: State the expected behavior before writing implementation code.
Run the focused test once to confirm it fails for the expected reason.
Keep each test small, clear, and focused on user-visible behavior.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation first and adding tests afterward.
Asserting that a mock exists instead of testing real behavior.
Adding production methods that only exist to support tests.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests before code?
faq.answer: Yes. The core workflow requires a failing test before production implementation code.

faq.question: Can I use it for bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for a regression test that fails before the fix is written.

faq.question: Does it support specific test frameworks?
faq.answer: It gives general TDD guidance and TypeScript examples, but it does not install or configure frameworks.

faq.question: Does it allow mocks?
faq.answer: Yes, but only when needed. It warns against testing mock behavior instead of real behavior.

faq.question: Is it safe for existing codebases?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill encourages deletion of non-TDD work, so removal should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
